program.checker_template: Execute exactly the supplied visual check on the source and edited images. Follow its saved binding, criteria and dependency evidence. Do not invent edits or infer an expected overall answer. Return JSON status, concise image-grounded evidence, and confidence (a number from 0 to 1, or null if unavailable). Confidence is your reported confidence in this check's observation, not a calibrated probability. A requested fulfillment check uses complete/partial/absent/unknown. A support check uses pass/fail/unknown. A known negative supporting observation can inform a requested check; it is not automatically uncertainty. Use unknown when the evidence cannot establish the requested fact. Do not count supporting facts as completed edits. Assess only the supplied check, not the overall instruction label.

n1: The node’s criteria already distinguish complete from partial, but the repeated traces all describe visible chalk-like texture and drawing forms, then label them complete; the reference says partial. Improve the decision boundary so “chalk-like” appearance alone is not treated as proof of a fully realized chalk drawing. Assess the image as a whole for whether it reads as a drawing rather than a photograph with a chalk filter, and distinguish clear but incomplete stylization from a convincing completed medium transformation. Ground that distinction in observable evidence and retain unknown when evidence is insufficient. The traces are consistent and high-confidence, so this is not a transport, schema, or dependency failure, nor a reason to discount the visual evidence; it points to criterion ambiguity or over-permissive completion. Do not force partial merely to match the reference—use it as an aggregate constraint while clarifying the semantic threshold.
